sources.title: National Climate Change Policy for Grenada, Carriacou and Petite Martinique
sources.organization: Government of Grenada, Ministry of Climate Resilience, Environment and Renewable Energy
sources.temporal_coverage: Draft sets policy priorities for an indicated 2025–2035 period; filename instead labels 2025–2030; historical indicators through 2024.
sources.methodology: Government policy summarizes climate risks and proposes objectives.
sources.limitations: Draft status is unconfirmed; filename says 2025–2030, cover 2025–2035; figures are not re-tested.

sources.title: Grenada: National case study on drought vulnerability and impact assessment
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical drought cases through 2024; socioeconomic and infrastructure indicators span different reference years.
sources.methodology: FAO profile compiles national drought-impact and vulnerability information with listed references.
sources.limitations: The web profile combines indicators from different years and is not a household survey or causal estimate.

sources.title: Water Availability
sources.organization: Government of Grenada, Ministry of Climate Resilience, Environment and Renewable Energy
sources.temporal_coverage: Water supply, governance and climate-risk information; numerical indicators are undated on the page.
sources.methodology: Ministry portal summarizes water availability, sector governance and climate risks.
sources.limitations: The page gives no visible publication date or method for the numerical supply estimates.

sources.title: NAWASA highlights major water security investments in Carriacou as G-CREWS project concludes
sources.organization: National Water and Sewerage Authority (NAWASA), Grenada
sources.temporal_coverage: G-CREWS delivery reported through October 2026, including post-Beryl investments and remaining operational works.
sources.methodology: Utility corporate account reports project outputs and attributed statements from government and project officials.
sources.limitations: Implementer-reported outputs; the account does not independently evaluate sustained service or livelihood outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF p. 24, printed p. 24, Socio-Economic Factors
claims.paraphrase: The draft places 2020 poverty risk highest in St. Mark and St. Andrew (54.8% nationally); poorer households often lack emergency funds and secure housing.
claims.limitations: The poverty figures describe 2020 and are not current estimates.

claims.locator: PDF p. 26, printed p. 26, Priority Vulnerable Groups, Female Headed Households
claims.paraphrase: The draft says nearly half of households are female-headed and women and children face higher post-disaster gender-based-violence risk, particularly in emergency shelters.
claims.limitations: The draft states a risk, not a measured count of post-Beryl incidents.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Draft links post-disaster GBV risk to emergency shelters.

claims.locator: PDF p. 10, Foreword, community stability and climate mobility
claims.paraphrase: The foreword calls climate change a national-security concern threatening essential services and community stability, and flags forced displacement and migration as an emerging climate-mobility issue.
claims.limitations: These are policy risk statements, not measured displacement, conflict or violence outcomes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Draft links climate impacts to community stability and forced mobility.

claims.locator: PDF p. 11, Executive Summary, implementation gaps
claims.paraphrase: Stakeholder consultations identify limited staff, slow procurement, coordination difficulties and overlapping agency mandates as implementation barriers.
claims.limitations: The policy does not quantify these constraints by locality or service.

claims.locator: Historical Drought and Drought Impact Pathway sections
claims.paraphrase: FAO identifies Carriacou, Petite Martinique, southern and southeastern mainland Grenada, and the drier north as drought-affected areas, with water scarcity straining tourism, agriculture and local supplies.
claims.limitations: The profile does not provide a comparable recent parish-level drought ranking.

claims.locator: Drought Impact Pathway, livestock and banana impacts
claims.paraphrase: FAO reports Carriacou livestock losses of 20% and 40% in the 1984 and 1992 droughts, and a 17% decline in national banana production during the 2009 drought.
claims.limitations: These are historical losses, not current impact estimates.

claims.locator: Drought Impact Pathway, gendered water-shortage impacts
claims.paraphrase: FAO says water shortages disproportionately affect women and girls through missed work or school, compromised hygiene and added care for sick relatives.
claims.limitations: The page provides no survey date or disaggregated count for these impacts.

claims.locator: Water Availability, Challenges and Opportunities; Water Resources
claims.paraphrase: The Ministry reports mainland dry-season daily yield of 31,800 m³ against demand of 54,600 m³; 91% of households in Carriacou and Petite Martinique use cisterns as main storage.
claims.limitations: The portal gives no visible reference date or method for these supply estimates.

claims.locator: Water Availability, Water Governance and Policy Framework
claims.paraphrase: The Ministry says water responsibilities are split among agencies without a single sector-wide oversight entity; the 2020 Water Policy proposed separate resource-management oversight.
claims.limitations: A proposed oversight entity is not evidence it was later established.

claims.locator: Article paragraphs on storage tanks, service continuity and remaining operational works
claims.paraphrase: NAWASA reports two 100,000-gallon tanks commissioned at Belair and Mt. Royal; their combined capacity is expected to provide three to six days of storage.
claims.limitations: The storage buffer is an estimate; interconnections, pumping and commissioning works remained before full benefits.

claims.locator: Article paragraphs on Mt. Royal rainwater harvesting and health facilities
claims.paraphrase: NAWASA says the Mt. Royal communal rainwater retrofit serves about 56 households and 169 residents; storage was also added at Princess Royal Hospital and two medical stations.
claims.limitations: The implementer reports infrastructure outputs, not sustained service reliability.

claims.locator: Article paragraphs on the G-CREWS Challenge Fund for Agriculture
claims.paraphrase: NAWASA reports over 300 farmers benefited across the tri-island state; on Carriacou, 18 received drip or micro-sprinkler support and 22 gained over 60,000 gallons of harvesting storage; 19 shade houses remain in phased installation.
claims.limitations: Provider-reported reach; the shade houses are in phased installation, not reported as complete.

access_audit.notes: Opened and read the public Ministry portal page, including its supply estimates and governance summary.

access_audit.notes: Opened and read NAWASA's 11 October 2026 project account; claims remain attributed to the utility.

access_audit.notes: The official PDF returned HTTP 403; no search-indexed or secondary text was used for claims.

access_audit.notes: Official landing page was readable, but the linked 15.6 MB PDF exceeded the browser text-fetch limit; no report claims were used.
The public IFRC-linked assessment cover marks the document Internal; its substantive contents were excluded.

search_audit.query: Grenada drought vulnerability subnational Carriacou Petite Martinique parish report climate risks
search_audit.outcome: Opened FAO's national drought profile and the Government draft climate policy; they identify sister-island, northern, southeastern and named-parish vulnerabilities, but do not provide a current comprehensive local ranking.

search_audit.query: Grenada climate change conflict violence migration displacement gender-based violence official report
search_audit.outcome: The draft policy names climate mobility, forced displacement and post-disaster shelter GBV risks; no opened report establishes armed conflict or a countrywide climate-to-violence effect.

search_audit.query: Grenada insecurity conflict armed violence disrupting climate adaptation disaster recovery water services
search_audit.outcome: No accessible country-specific source linked insecurity or conflict to disrupted climate adaptation or service delivery; the draft policy lists administrative implementation barriers without attributing them to insecurity.

search_audit.query: Grenada climate resilience water drought early warning adaptation capacity Carriacou project assessment
search_audit.outcome: Opened official water-availability information and NAWASA's G-CREWS close-out account; they report water governance constraints and delivered storage, health-facility and farm investments, with some works still pending.

gaps: The official IOM climate-mobility assessment returned HTTP 403 and the Government-led Beryl PDNA PDF exceeded the browser fetch limit; no claims use indexed summaries.
A publicly linked IFRC rapid assessment was marked Internal on its cover and excluded; the WFP BRISP report PDF presented a bot-verification page.
No accessible country-specific source connected armed conflict or insecurity with climate impacts or adaptation delivery; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
The Government climate policy file is a December draft; its risk statements and proposed actions are not treated as adopted or measured outcomes.
These sources do not establish a countrywide causal estimate of climate-related conflict or violence.
